blogTitle: New Lab Analytics Dashboards, With Options for Every Plan
elevenlabsPodcastSourceText:
This is a Confident LIMS product brief, read using AI voice generation.

Confident LIMS has launched a new set of Analytics dashboards, with options on every plan. Lab-specific dashboards use your lab account's own data. Premium benchmarks add aggregated, privacy-screened market data. Everything refreshes daily at midnight Pacific Time, covering samples from January first, twenty twenty-four onward.

First, see where samples spend time. You can see how long samples sit in each assay status, which statuses take the longest, and how long in-progress samples have been open. Average and median time in assay statuses live on separate dashboards, so you can compare the two. One thing worth knowing: Overdue Samples shows samples that were already published late. It is a record, not a prediction.

Second, spot changes in your test results. Track analyte averages, variation, and failure rates by assay, matrix, package, client, or date. These views are built on published results, so a change in an average or a failure rate is a reason to investigate, not a finding in itself. The variation metric divides the standard deviation by the mean, so it stays comparable across analytes at very different concentrations.

Third, bring evidence to your client conversations. Use client filters where available to review an account's volume, revenue, turnaround time, and test-result trends. Not every dashboard carries a client filter, but the account-level ones do.

Fourth, see where your volume and revenue concentrate. The market dashboards show where volume, revenue, and active clients sit across your book of business. On Premium, market benchmarks let you compare your pricing, turnaround time, and failure rates against aggregated, privacy-screened market data.

Fifth, review unpaid order balances by client, geography, and time since order receipt, with order-level detail behind every number. This is order aging, counted from when the order came in, not invoice aging.

What's included depends on your plan. Starter and Basic labs get built-in dashboards for core sample volume and revenue. Pro labs get Advanced Analytics, including test results, pricing, inventory, client dashboards, and maps, with workflow tracking for Pro and Premium LIMS labs. Premium labs get everything above plus market benchmarks.

If you're a Confident customer, log in today and open Analytics. If you're not yet, visit confidentlims dot com slash get-started. Link in the show notes. Thanks for listening.
elevenlabsNarrationScript:
This article was written by Confident LIMS and is being read to you using AI voice generation.

New Lab Analytics Dashboards, With Options for Every Plan.

Every lab already has the data. It's sitting in sample records, test results, invoices, and client accounts. The problem is that turning it into a decision usually means exporting to a spreadsheet, building the same pivot table again, and hoping nobody changed a column name.

That changes today. Confident LIMS, a Laboratory Information Management System, now includes a new set of Analytics dashboards, with options on every plan. They cover the questions lab managers ask every week: where samples spend their time, how test results are trending, what's happening with each client, where your volume and revenue concentrate, and which order balances are still unpaid.

In short: the new Confident Analytics dashboards give analytical testing labs a shared view of turnaround time, test-result trends, client activity, market position, and unpaid order balances, without exporting anything. Lab-specific dashboards use your lab account's own data. Premium benchmarks add aggregated, privacy-screened market data. The dashboards refresh daily at midnight Pacific Time and cover samples from January first, twenty twenty-four onward.

Here's what your team can do with them.

See where samples spend time.

Turnaround time is the number your clients judge you on, and it's usually the last number anyone looks at. By the time a monthly report shows it creeping up, the samples that caused it are long gone.

The workflow dashboards make that visible earlier. You can see how long samples sit in each assay status, which statuses take the longest, and how long in-progress samples have been open. Average and median time in assay statuses live on separate dashboards, so you can compare the two and tell everyday friction apart from one-off outliers. A single rerun that took nine days shouldn't look like a systemic problem, and a steady two-hour drift shouldn't hide behind a good average.

One thing worth knowing: Overdue Samples shows samples that were already published late. It's a record of what happened, not a prediction of what's about to. Read it as the scoreboard, and use the in-progress views to see what's still in play.

The dashboards here are Turnaround Time, In-Progress Samples Aging, and Overdue Samples.

Spot changes in your test results.

Shifts in test results rarely announce themselves. They show up as a slow move in an analyte average, a widening spread on one matrix, or a failure rate that ticks up for a single client's product line.

You can now track analyte averages, variation, and failure rates by assay, matrix, package, client, or date. These views are built on published results, so what they show you is what your clients already received. A change in an average or a failure rate is a reason to go and look, not a finding in itself. The dashboards tell you where to point your investigation, and your QA process tells you what it means.

A note on the math: the variation metric divides the standard deviation by the mean, so it stays comparable across analytes that sit at very different concentrations.

The dashboards here are Analyte Values, Standard Deviation Analyte Values, and Failed Samples.

Bring evidence to your client conversations.

Most client check-ins run on anecdotes. Someone remembers that an account "seemed quieter lately" or that "they had a few fails last quarter." That's not a great way to protect revenue.

Use client filters where available to review an account's volume, revenue, turnaround time, and test-result trends. Your team walks into the conversation with something specific: which products are growing, which tests are failing, and whether your turnaround time for that client is holding up. Not every dashboard carries a client filter — inventory and market benchmark views work at a different level — but the account-level ones do.

The dashboards here are Active Clients, Churned Clients, and Sample Revenue.

See where your volume and revenue concentrate.

Where does your volume come from? Where does your revenue concentrate? Which regions have active clients and which ones don't? Those are strategy questions, and until now they took a spreadsheet and an afternoon.

The market dashboards show where volume, revenue, and active clients sit across your book of business. On Premium, market benchmarks go further: you can compare your pricing, turnaround time, and failure rates against aggregated, privacy-screened market data. If a region is paying more for slower results, that's a market worth a closer look.

The dashboards here are Market Share, Market Benchmarks, and the Revenue, Volume, and Active Clients Maps.

Review unpaid order balances.

Unpaid balances are a lab problem as much as a finance problem. Every unanswered "what do we owe you?" email costs someone on your team a detour through the billing system.

Review unpaid order balances by client, geography, and time since order receipt, with order-level detail behind every number. Note that this is order aging, not invoice aging: balances are counted from when the order came in, not from an invoice date or payment terms. Your billing team can answer a client's question in the same call, without building another spreadsheet.

The dashboards here are Receivables, Receivables Schedules, and Order Revenue.

What's included in your plan.

There are options on every plan, and what you get depends on your tier. Starter and Basic labs get built-in dashboards covering core sample volume and revenue. Pro labs get Advanced Analytics dashboards, including test results, pricing, inventory, client dashboards, and maps. Workflow tracking, the assay-status views, is available to Pro and Premium LIMS labs; API-only labs don't run assay-status workflows, so those dashboards don't apply. Premium labs get everything above plus market benchmarks: aggregated, privacy-screened data for comparing your operations across regions and industries.

Lab-specific dashboards use your lab account's own data. Premium benchmarks add aggregated, privacy-screened market data, so you can see the market without anyone seeing you.

Frequently asked questions.

Do I need to set anything up to use the new dashboards? No. They're live in your Confident account and built from the data your lab already records. Log in and open Analytics.

How current is the data? Dashboards refresh daily at midnight Pacific Time, and sample history runs from January first, twenty twenty-four onward. They're a daily operating view rather than a live monitor.

Which plans include Advanced Analytics and benchmarks? Advanced Analytics is Pro and Premium. Market benchmarks are Premium only. Starter and Basic include the built-in sample volume and revenue dashboards.

Can other labs see my data in the market benchmarks? No. Benchmarks are aggregated and privacy-screened. They add market context without exposing any individual lab's data, including yours.

Can I filter dashboards by client? Where available, yes. Account-level dashboards carry client filters for volume, revenue, turnaround time, and test-result trends. Inventory and market benchmark dashboards work at a different level and don't.

See it for yourself.

If you're a Confident customer, this update is already live in your account. Log in and explore, or read the step-by-step guide in our help center. Link in the show notes.

If you're still running your lab on exports and pivot tables, this is a good week to see what a LIMS built for analytical testing looks like.

Questions? Reach us at support at confidentlims dot com.

To see it in action, visit confidentlims dot com slash get-started, or find the link in the show notes. Thanks for listening.
episodeDescription:
Confident LIMS just launched a new set of Analytics dashboards for analytical testing labs, with options on every plan. This short brief is for lab managers, QA leads, and lab owners who would rather run the lab on their own numbers than on another spreadsheet export.

You'll hear where the workflow dashboards show samples spending their time, how the test-result views track analyte averages, variation, and failure rates on published results, how client and market views turn weekly guesswork into something specific, and what's included on Starter, Basic, Pro, and Premium.
